posts.text:
A worsening drought in South Sudan, driven in part by the ongoing El Niño, is putting lives and livelihoods at risk.

I’ve allocated $6M from UN’s Global Emergency Fund CERF to support early action, including food, health, nutrition, protection, water and sanitation services.

In Zimbabwe, the forecasts are in. Prolonged dry spells are coming. El Niño is bearing down.

$4M from UN’s Global Emergency Fund CERF for anticipatory action will help get food, health and nutrition in before the drought arrives, not after it destroys.

“We have been testing anticipatory action in Chad. And it works.”

@OnuTchad Humanitarian Coordinator @fbatalingaya explains how the UN Global Emergency Fund CERF is supporting anticipatory action in Chad to help families protect livelihoods and cope better with droughts.

In #Kenya, over 4 million people are facing hunger due to prolonged drought.

With support from the OCHA-managed Kenya Humanitarian Fund, @UN and partners are life-saving support to families.

With potential El Niño impacts ahead, acting early to help communities prepare is key.

Severe El Niño-related dry conditions are forecast across Madagascar’s Grand Sud, threatening a deterioration in food security.

I’ve allocated $6M from the UN’s Global Emergency Fund CERF for anticipatory action to help communities prepare.

A severe drought linked to the latest El Niño event is expected to worsen food security in Djibouti, putting many lives at risk.

I’ve allocated $2M from the UN’s Global Emergency Fund CERF for anticipatory action in food and nutrition, protection, and water and sanitation.

In #SouthSudan, the UN and partners are supporting preparedness efforts against Ebola, floods and drought.

Health partners have screened more than 135,300 travellers this month, while plans are in place to strengthen early action.

Read more: https://bit.ly/4wagFTx

Communities still recovering from the last El Niño could be hit again this year.

Floods. Drought. Hunger. Disease. Displacement. Across Southern and Eastern Africa.

8 things to know about what’s coming – and why early action is the only answer.

https://bit.ly/4yUMItv

The efforts of families bear fruit when support arrives on time: the fertilizer from the #CERFAA Project strengthened the plot. Today they transform corn into tamales and elotes, generating income that strengthens their livelihoods in the face of drought.

posts.theme: Climate crisis / glacier and mountain risk
posts.text: In Hunza, I heard the way that the direct danger from climate crisis is changing the vocabulary of communities.

The first results are already visible. Testimonies from families show how drip irrigation and community work strengthen crops and livelihoods, demonstrating that getting ahead protects production and ensures food in the face of drought.
Adama received support to help protect her children from disease before floods peaked in Nigeria. Mehreen reached hospital and delivered her baby safely during floods

Anticipatory actions: community leaders are trained in land preparation and installation of drip irrigation. “All the neighbors come to learn how to cultivate and sow during times of drought,” shares Erlinda Cruz in El Común.

@OCHAFunds

Leaders were trained in the installation and management of drip irrigation systems. They will pass on what they have learned to their communities. “Today we feel accompanied and supported to sow with hope,” shares María López in Hato Quemado.

@OCHAFunds

115 families received drip irrigation kits. These #AnticipatoryActions ensure food and strengthen resilience. “We must reinforce mechanisms that make families more resilient,” highlights Fátima Espinal, FAO Honduras.

@OCHAFunds

The #AccionesAnticipatorias strengthen the resilience of 2,500 families in the Dry Corridor. Drought- and pest-resistant seeds ensure food and livelihoods. “It’s a blessing for our community,” says Lorena in Malagua.

@OCHAFunds

Before the drought puts the meal on the table at risk, anticipating saves lives. In Jalapa, with #CERF and #AccionesAnticipatorias, WFP supported with transfers and nutrition messages.
@UNOCHA @OCHAFunds @UNOCHA_Americas @SecretariaSESAN @MagaGuatemala @WFP_es

As climate change intensifies, climate shocks are becoming more dangerous and more unpredictable. The world already knows what El Niño can do. The question now is whether we act early – or explain later why we didn’t.

The UN Global Emergency Fund CERF is helping turn forecasts into early action.

Across multiple countries, #anticipatoryaction is enabling communities to prepare before climate shocks hit – reducing risks and protecting lives.

Read more
https://bit.ly/4wlHBRB

posts.country: Burkina Faso; Cuba; Fiji; Mozambique; Nigeria; Philippines
posts.text: Climate shocks are accelerating. So is early humanitarian action. But across Burkina Faso, Cuba, Fiji, Mozambique, Nigeria and the Philippines, governments and communities are showing that acting before disaster strikes can save lives, protect livelihoods and preserve dignity. From floods and cyclones to hurricanes and typhoons, anticipatory action is helping people prepare, respond faster and reduce harm before crises escalate. Swipe through to read from the people leading and delivering anticipatory action on the ground.

When Cyclone Gezani threatened Madagascar, humanitarian action started before its landfall. Funding from the UN’s Global Emergency Fund CERF was released ahead of the cyclone, helping communities receive life-saving assistance in time. Together, the Government, UN agencies and NGOs prepared communities and delivered support faster when it mattered most. Early action saves lives.

Funding from the UN’s Global Emergency Fund CERF was released ahead of the cyclone, helping communities receive life-saving assistance in time.

Together, the Government, UN agencies and NGOs prepared communities and delivered support faster when it mattered most.

Early action saves lives.

Faryab is one of many parts of #Afghanistan where drought has hit four of the past five years. This has caused rising hunger, disease and families struggling to keep farms alive. The Afghanistan Humanitarian Fund and UN's Global Emergency Fund CERF have joined forces on anticipatory action – helping communities prepare before the worst impacts of the drought hits their communities. This allows partners to invest in longer-term solutions providing livelihoods, water and agriculture.

I’m in eastern #DRC, where over 20 million people need support.

We’re planning ahead to stop deadly cholera outbreaks before they escalate – saving lives, time and resources.

Humanitarians call this anticipatory action.

The @UN’s global emergency fund, @UNCERF, leads the way in #AnticipatoryAction, reaching millions of people before disasters strike.

The result?
Faster, more effective & more dignified humanitarian action.

See how CERF helped people on the frontline of the climate crisis.

A race against the clock in #Bangladesh.

In 2024, @UNCERF released funds for flood response in just 16 minutes.

Watch to find out how this helped people.

🌊When disasters strike, it's often too late. But what if we could act before they hit? In Bangladesh, #AnticipatoryAction backed by the UN's Emergency Fund, CERF, helped 430,000 people prepare for floods before the worst came – delivering cash, clean water and safety in just 5 days. This is the power of planning ahead.💪

At today’s roundtable hosted by Norway on Anticipatory Action, the message is clear: acting early saves lives, time and money.

It’s at heart of the humanitarian reset – more local, ready for tomorrow’s crises.

Let’s fund it and scale it.

https://bit.ly/3GGILC2

"Anticipatory action is at the heart of the renewal of the international system," says UN Relief Chief, Tom Fletcher. Anticipatory action 🟠saves money 🟠saves time 🟠saves lives Every $1 spent on anticipatory action can save up to $7 in losses. It helps communities better prepare for predictable crises. Smart, effective, and worth the investment. See the evidence for yourself: https://bit.ly/3GGILC2

In Afghanistan, the climate emergency is real.

As part of the humanitarian reset, we must be smarter, more innovative and local. We have used anticipatory action to unlock $16.6M to help people get ahead of future crises.

Head of OCHA Ethiopia Paul Handley visits Borena Zone, where funding from the Ethiopia Humanitarian Fund & @UNCERF enabled anticipatory action ahead of predicted drought.

Find out how early interventions like sustained access to water & livestock support protect communities.

posts.text: In Bangladesh, the #AnticipatoryAction triggers for floods in the Jamuna River basin have been reached, prompting an immediate disbursement of up to $6.2 million

Proactive measures ahead of a severe drought in #Niger helped 160K people avoid significant hardship.

Thanks to a $9.5M anticipatory action allocation from @UNCERF, communities were able to act before the shock, securing grazing, staying healthy and keeping their kids in school.

Timor-Leste faces an imminent and severe drought due to El Niño. @UNReliefChief has allocated $2.08M from @UNCERF to kick-start the response, scale up #anticipatoryaction before the drought and to help people already in need. #InvestInHumanity

Acting early ahead of disasters helps communities prepare and protect themselves from the devastating consequences.

Since 2020, @UNCERF has allocated $90 million to support #AnticipatoryAction in 19 countries grappling with humanitarian emergencies.

#InvestInHumanity

In #Somalia, seasonal rains are causing significant flash floods.

In Baidoa, at least 122k people - most of whom are already internally displaced - have been affected.

Humanitarians are working with the Government on emergency response, preparedness & anticipatory action.

For the second time this year, Anticipatory Action from @UNCERF is making a difference in #DRCongo.

With an allocation of $750k, we’re proactively fighting #cholera.

This will help protect 100k+ people, providing early detection, safe water, sanitation & medical care.

Do you know what #AnticipatoryAction is?

Many extreme weather events are now predictable. This makes it possible to trigger anticipatory action – acting before a predicted disaster.

Humanitarians did exactly that in Nepal, Niger and South Sudan: http://bit.ly/46ipjnj

Climate change is unpredictable, but Anticipatory Action isn’t.

Harnessing tech & analytics, we’re helping vulnerable communities in Nepal, Niger and South Sudan prepare for the worst.

Better preparation = reduced impact.

Read how: https://bit.ly/46ipjnj

Australia’s generous support to @UNCERF and @CBPFs enables partners to assist people in dire need worldwide.
